summary: Backend-only Phase 1 end-to-end tests against LIVE dev DB via external URL. Wrote pytest suite covering all 20 requested scenarios: health, OTP send-rate-limit, verify-OTP (seeded manager + wrong-OTP + unknown-phone), refresh, /me, public departments (13, trilingual), forms list scoping, form submit happy + invalid-select, manager approval, worker submission scoping, incident create + timeline + worker-403 + manager-status-change + CGM-cross-dept-visibility, attendance verified_plus / verified / flagged / duplicate-409, flagged-list role scoping, dashboard summary, /shifts/mine (8 days), shift-swap same-shift 400 + cross-dept 400, file upload PNG serve + .exe rejection, admin PATCH settings CGM-ok/worker-403, notifications incident_assigned present + mark-read. Result: 20 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. The 3 skips are the first-time-punch-in variants (verified_plus / verified / flagged) which returned 409 because those worker phones had already punched in today on an earlier run — this is the expected persistence behavior explicitly called out by the main agent (unique (employee, day) constraint on Attendance). A rerun after DB cleanup would exercise them; on the very first execution of this suite (before any 409 was possible) all three PASSED with the correct verification_level ('verified_plus', 'verified', 'flagged').

critical_code_review_comments: Routing, RBAC (rank<=2 / ==3 / >3) and cross-department scoping are correctly enforced across forms, submissions, incidents, attendance, and admin.

Attendance verification_level tiering (verified_plus / verified / flagged / gps_missing) matches spec; duplicate-day 409 is enforced both by Python check AND the DB unique constraint, so races are safe.
Auth flow: OTP rate limit (3/10min) uses Redis INCR + EXPIRE — correct. Wrong-OTP lockout counter and demo-OTP override behave correctly.
Files router: extension allowlist + 10 MB cap + UUID keys; serve endpoint validates key via LocalStorage.path_for(). Solid.
Notifications correctly created for incident_assigned on incident creation (verified end-to-end).
